## 2. Folyamatos integráció (CI)  

**Fájl:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`  

```yaml
name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  lint-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:15
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: ai_user
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ai_pass
          POSTGRES_DB: ai_engineer
        ports: ["5432:5432"]
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U $$POSTGRES_USER"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # ---------- Lint Go ----------
      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v4
        with:
          go-version: "1.22"
      - name: Go mod tidy
        run: |
          cd services/orchestrator
          go mod tidy
      - name: Go lint
        run: |
          go install golang.org/x/lint/golint@latest
          golint ./...

      # ---------- Lint Python ----------
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install Python deps
        run: |
          cd services/planner
          pip install -e .
          pip install ruff
      - name: Ruff lint
        run: |
          cd services/planner
          ruff check .

      # ---------- Lint Rust ----------
      - name: Install Rust
        uses: actions-rs/toolchain@v1
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          profile: minimal
          override: true
      - name: Cargo fmt & clippy
        run: |
          cd services/toolchain
          cargo fmt -- --check
          cargo clippy -- -D warnings

      # ---------- Lint Node ----------
      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"
      - name: Install Node deps
        run: |
          cd services/testing_agent
          npm ci
      - name: ESLint
        run: |
          cd services/testing_agent
          npx eslint .

      # ---------- Unit Tests ----------
      - name: Go unit tests
        run: |
          cd services/orchestrator
          go test ./...

      - name: Python unit tests
        run: |
          cd services/planner
          pytest -q

      - name: Rust unit tests
        run: |
          cd services/toolchain
          cargo test --quiet

      - name: Node unit tests
        run: |
          cd services/testing_agent
          npm test --silent
```

## 3. Infrastruktúra – Terraform  

Az összes infrastruktúra a Google Cloud Platformon (GCP) fut. A Terraform modullal egy VPC‑t, GKE‑klustert, CloudSQL‑t (PostgreSQL), Artifact Registry‑t a konténerképekhez, valamint egy menedzselt Temporal szervert (Helm‑en) hozunk létre.  

**Fájl:** `infra/terraform/main.tf`  

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.6"
  required_providers {
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
    kubernetes = {
      source  = "hashicorp/kubernetes"
      version = "~> 2.26"
    }
  }
}

provider "google" {
  project = var.gcp_project
  region  = var.gcp_region
}

# -------------------------------------------------
# VPC & Subnet
# -------------------------------------------------
resource "google_compute_network" "vpc" {
  name                    = "ai-engineer-vpc"
  auto_create_subnetworks = false
}

resource "google_compute_subnetwork" "subnet" {
  name          = "ai-engineer-subnet"
  ip_cidr_range = "10.2.0.0/16"
  region        = var.gcp_region
  network       = google_compute_network.vpc.id
}

# -------------------------------------------------
# GKE Cluster (autoscaling, warm node pools)
# -------------------------------------------------
resource "google_container_cluster" "primary" {
  name               = "ai-engineer-gke"
  location           = var.gcp_region
  networking_mode    = "VPC_NATIVE"
  network            = google_compute_network.vpc.id
  subnetwork         = google_compute_subnetwork.subnet.id

  remove_default_node_pool = true
  initial_node_count       = 1

  release_channel {
    channel = "STABLE"
  }

  workload_identity_config {
    identity_namespace = "${var.gcp_project}.svc.id.goog"
  }

  autoscaling {
    enabled = true
    min_node_count = 3
    max_node_count = 30
  }

  node_pool {
    name       = "warm-pool"
    initial_node_count = 3
    autoscaling {
      min_node_count = 3
      max_node_count = 15
    }
    management {
      auto_repair  = true
      auto_upgrade = true
    }
    node_config {
      machine_type = "e2-standard-4"
      oauth_scopes = [
        ""
      ]
    }
  }
}

# -------------------------------------------------
# CloudSQL PostgreSQL (high‑availability)
# -------------------------------------------------
resource "google_sql_database_instance" "postgres" {
  name             = "ai-engineer-pg"
  database_version = "POSTGRES_15"
  region           = var.gcp_region
  settings {
    tier = "db-custom-2-8192"
    availability_type = "REGIONAL"
    backup_configuration {
      enabled = true
    }
    ip_configuration {
      ipv4_enabled    = false
      private_network = google_compute_network.vpc.id
    }
  }
}

resource "google_sql_user" "db_user" {
  name     = "ai_user"
  instance = google_sql_database_instance.postgres.name
  password = var.db_password
}

resource "google_sql_database" "app_db" {
  name     = "ai_engineer"
  instance = google_sql_database_instance.postgres.name
  charset  = "UTF8"
  collation = "en_US.UTF8"
}

# -------------------------------------------------
# Artifact Registry for container images
# -------------------------------------------------
resource "google_artifact_registry_repository" "repo" {
  location      = var.gcp_region
  repository_id = "ai-engineer-repo"
  format        = "DOCKER"
  description   = "Container images for AI Engineer services"
}

# -------------------------------------------------
# Temporal Helm Release (managed within GKE)
# -------------------------------------------------
resource "kubernetes_namespace" "temporal" {
  metadata {
    name = "temporal"
  }
}

resource "helm_release" "temporal" {
  name       = "temporal"
  repository = ""
  chart      = "temporal"
  namespace  = kubernetes_namespace.temporal.metadata[0].name
  version    = "1.22.0"

  set {
    name  = "server.persistence.sql.password"
    value = var.db_password
  }
  set {
    name  = "server.persistence.sql.host"
    value = google_sql_database_instance.postgres.private_ip_address
  }
  set {
    name  = "server.persistence.sql.database"
    value = google_sql_database.app_db.name
  }
  set {
    name  = "server.replication.taskQueues"
    value = "3"
  }
}
```

### 4.3 Entrypoint script  

**Fájl:** `infra/docker/entrypoint.sh`  

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Export common env vars
export TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE="${TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE:-default}"
export POSTGRES_DSN="postgres://ai_user:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@${POSTGRES_HOST}:5432/ai_engineer?sslmode=disable"
```

```go
// Workflow represents a single 200‑minute autonomous session.
func AgentWorkflow(ctx workflow.Context, sessionID string) error {
logger := workflow.GetLogger(ctx)
logger.Info("Starting Agent session", "sessionID", sessionID)

// 1. Initialize planner
pa := workflow.NewPromise(ctx)
ctx = workflow.WithChildOptions(ctx, workflow.ChildWorkflowOptions{
WorkflowID: "planner-" + sessionID,
WorkflowRunTimeout: time.Hour * 4,
})
workflow.ExecuteChildWorkflow(ctx, PlannerWorkflow, sessionID).Get(ctx, pa)

select {
case <-ctx.Done():
logger.Info("Session timeout / cancellation")
return ctx.Err()

return err

workflow.ExecuteChildWorkflow(ctx, PlannerWorkflow, sessionID).Get(ctx, pa)
}
}
```

**Fájl:** `services/planner/src/planner.py`  

```python
import os
import uuid
import json
import asyncio
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
from openai import OpenAI
from decision_guidance import DecisionGuidance

app = FastAPI()
client = OpenAI(api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"))
guidance = DecisionGuidance(model_path="/config/policy/decision_guidance.yaml")

class SessionRequest(BaseModel):
    user_prompt: str
    session_id: str = None

class PlannerResponse(BaseModel):
    task_id: str
    task_type: str   # "test", "tool", "deploy"
    payload: dict

def generate_task_id() -> str:
    return str(uuid.uuid4())

async def decompose_prompt(prompt: str) -> list[PlannerResponse]:
    # Call LLM to split prompt into atomic tasks.
    system_prompt = """You are an AI software engineer. Decompose the user's request into ordered atomic tasks.
    Each task must be one of: "write_code", "run_test", "run_tool", "deploy". Return a JSON array where each element has:
    { "task_id": "<uuid>", "task_type": "<type>", "payload": { ... } }."""
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=[{"role":"system","content":system_prompt},
                  {"role":"user","content":prompt}],
        temperature=0.0,
        response_format={"type":"json_object"}
    )
    tasks_json = json.loads(response.choices[0].message.content)
    return [PlannerResponse(**t) for t in tasks_json]

@app.post("/plan", response_model=PlannerResponse)
async def plan(request: SessionRequest):
    session_id = request.session_id or generate_task_id()
    # Decision‑time guidance may block or modify the request.
    allowed, micro_instr = guidance.evaluate(request.user_prompt, session_id)
    if not allowed:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Policy blocked request")
    if micro_instr:
        # micro‑instruction can be sent back for client‑side handling
        # (e.g., “use safe file write”, “avoid network call to X”)
        pass
    tasks = await decompose_prompt(request.user_prompt)
    # Return the first task; the orchestrator will request next tasks later.
    return tasks[0]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)
```

**Fájl:** `services/planner/src/decision_guidance.py`  

```python
import yaml
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

class DecisionGuidance:
    """
    Lightweight multi‑label classifier that decides whether a user prompt is allowed
    and optionally returns a short micro‑instruction (max 2 sentences).
    The model is loaded from a YAML file containing feature definitions and weights.
    """

    def __init__(self, model_path: str):
        with open(model_path, "r") as f:
            cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)
        self.vectorizer = cfg["vectorizer"]
        self.model = LogisticRegression(**cfg["model_params"])
        self.model.coef_ = np.array(cfg["coefficients"])
        self.model.intercept_ = np.array(cfg["intercept"])
        self.micro_instructions = cfg["micro_instructions"]

    def _featurize(self, text: str) -> np.ndarray:
        # Very simple bag‑of‑words based on provided token list.
        tokens = self.vectorizer["tokens"]
        vec = np.array([text.lower().count(tok) for tok in tokens])
        return vec.reshape(1, -1)

    def evaluate(self, text: str, session_id: str):
        """
        Returns (allowed: bool, micro_instruction: str|None)
        """
        X = self._featurize(text)
        prob = self.model.predict_proba(X)[0, 1]  # probability of "allow"
        if prob < self.vectorizer["allow_threshold"]:
            return False, None
        # Choose micro‑instruction probabilistically based on confidence.
        if prob < 0.9:
            instr = np.random.choice(self.micro_instructions["caution"])
        elif prob > 0.99:
            instr = np.random.choice(self.micro_instructions["optimistic"])
        else:
            instr = None
        return True, instr
```

```rust
use anyhow::Result;
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::fs;
use uuid::Uuid;

/// Represents a generic tool request coming from the orchestrator.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ToolRequest {
    pub id: String,
    pub tool_type: String,      // "edit", "run", "build"
    pub parameters: serde_json::Value,
}

/// Returns a JSON‑encoded response for the orchestrator.
pub async fn execute_tool(req: ToolRequest) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    match req.tool_type.as_str() {
        "edit" => edit_file(req).await,
        "run" => run_repl(req).await,
        "build" => run_build(req).await,
        _ => Err(anyhow::anyhow!("Unsupported tool_type")),
    }
}

async fn edit_file(req: ToolRequest) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    let path = req.parameters["path"]
        .as_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Missing path"))?;
    let content = req.parameters["content"]
        .as_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Missing content"))?;
    fs::write(path, content)?;
    Ok(serde_json::json!({"status":"ok"}))
}

async fn run_repl(req: ToolRequest) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    let language = req.parameters["language"]
        .as_str()
        .unwrap_or("python");
    let code = req.parameters["code"]
        .as_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Missing code"))?;

    // Simple REPL execution using subprocess.
    let output = Command::new(match language {
            "python" => "python3",
            "node" => "node",
            "bash" => "bash",
            _ => return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("Unsupported language")),
        })
        .arg("-c")
        .arg(code)
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
        .output()?;

    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
    Ok(serde_json::json!({
        "stdout": stdout,
        "stderr": stderr,
        "exit_code": output.status.code()
    }))
}

async fn run_build(_req: ToolRequest) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    // Trigger Nixpacks build via a CLI call.
    let status = Command::new("nixpacks")
        .arg("build")
        .arg("--config")
        .arg("/config/nixpacks")
        .status()?;
    Ok(serde_json::json!({"build_success": status.success()}))
}
```

```js
import { chromium } from "playwright";
import axios from "axios";

/**
 * Entry point called by the orchestrator via HTTP.
 * Expected payload:
 * {
 *   "taskId": "<uuid>",
 *   "previewUrl": "",
 *   "testPlan": "auto" // or explicit steps
 * }
 */
export async function run(task) {
  const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page = await context.newPage();

  // Video capture for observability
  await page.evaluate(() => console.log("Starting test run"));
  const videoPath = `/tmp/video-${task.taskId}.webm`;
  await context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true, sources: true });

  try {
    await page.goto(task.previewUrl, { waitUntil: "networkidle" });
    // Simple heuristic: click all buttons with non‑empty ARIA labels
    const buttons = await page.$$('[role="button"][aria-label]');
    for (const btn of buttons) {
      const label = await btn.getAttribute("aria-label");
      console.log(`Clicking button ${label}`);
      await btn.click({ force: true });
    }
    // Capture success state – look for a DOM element with data-test="ready"
    const ready = await page.$('[data-test="ready"]');
    const success = !!ready;
    await page.screenshot({ path: `/tmp/screenshot-${task.taskId}.png` });
    await context.tracing.stop({ path: `/tmp/trace-${task.taskId}.zip` });

    // Post result back to orchestrator
    await axios.post("", {
      taskId: task.taskId,
      success,
      videoPath,
      screenshotPath: `/tmp/screenshot-${task.taskId}.png`,
      tracePath: `/tmp/trace-${task.taskId}.zip`
    });
  } finally {
    await browser.close();
  }
}
```

```js
import { run } from "./index.js";
import http from "http";

const server = http.createServer(async (req, res) => {
  if (req.method !== "POST" || req.url !== "/run") {
    res.writeHead(404);
    res.end();
    return;
  }
  let body = "";
  req.on("data", (chunk) => (body += chunk));

    try {

      res.writeHead(500);

});
```

```python
import os
import uuid
import json
import asyncio
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
from openai import OpenAI
from decision_guidance import DecisionGuidance

app = FastAPI()
client = OpenAI(api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"))
guidance = DecisionGuidance(model_path="/config/policy/decision_guidance.yaml")

class SessionRequest(BaseModel):
    user_prompt: str
    session_id: str = None

class PlannerResponse(BaseModel):
    task_id: str
    task_type: str   # "test", "tool", "deploy"
    payload: dict

def generate_task_id() -> str:
    return str(uuid.uuid4())

async def decompose_prompt(prompt: str) -> list[PlannerResponse]:
    # Call LLM to split prompt into atomic tasks.
    system_prompt = """You are an AI software engineer. Decompose the user's request into ordered atomic tasks.
    Each task must be one of: "write_code", "run_test", "run_tool", "deploy". Return a JSON array where each element has:
    { "task_id": "<uuid>", "task_type": "<type>", "payload": { ... } }."""
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=[{"role":"system","content":system_prompt},
                  {"role":"user","content":prompt}],
        temperature=0.0,
        response_format={"type":"json_object"}
    )
    tasks_json = json.loads(response.choices[0].message.content)
    return [PlannerResponse(**t) for t in tasks_json]

@app.post("/plan", response_model=PlannerResponse)
async def plan(request: SessionRequest):
    session_id = request.session_id or generate_task_id()
    # Decision‑time guidance may block or modify the request.
    allowed, micro_instr = guidance.evaluate(request.user_prompt, session_id)
    if not allowed:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Policy blocked request")
    if micro_instr:
        # micro‑instruction can be sent back for client‑side handling
        # (e.g., “use safe file write”, “avoid network call to X”)
        pass
    tasks = await decompose_prompt(request.user_prompt)
    # Return the first task; the orchestrator will request next tasks later.
    return tasks[0]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)
```

```python
import yaml
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

class DecisionGuidance:
    """
    Lightweight multi‑label classifier that decides whether a user prompt is allowed
    and optionally returns a short micro‑instruction (max 2 sentences).
    The model is loaded from a YAML file containing feature definitions and weights.
    """

    def __init__(self, model_path: str):
        with open(model_path, "r") as f:
            cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)
        self.vectorizer = cfg["vectorizer"]
        self.model = LogisticRegression(**cfg["model_params"])
        self.model.coef_ = np.array(cfg["coefficients"])
        self.model.intercept_ = np.array(cfg["intercept"])
        self.micro_instructions = cfg["micro_instructions"]

    def _featurize(self, text: str) -> np.ndarray:
        # Very simple bag‑of‑words based on provided token list.
        tokens = self.vectorizer["tokens"]
        vec = np.array([text.lower().count(tok) for tok in tokens])
        return vec.reshape(1, -1)

    def evaluate(self, text: str, session_id: str):
        """
        Returns (allowed: bool, micro_instruction: str|None)
        """
        X = self._featurize(text)
        prob = self.model.predict_proba(X)[0, 1]  # probability of "allow"
        if prob < self.vectorizer["allow_threshold"]:
            return False, None
        # Choose micro‑instruction probabilistically based on confidence.
        if prob < 0.9:
            instr = np.random.choice(self.micro_instructions["caution"])
        elif prob > 0.99:
            instr = np.random.choice(self.micro_instructions["optimistic"])
        else:
            instr = None
        return True, instr
```

```rust
use anyhow::Result;
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::fs;
use uuid::Uuid;

/// Represents a generic tool request coming from the orchestrator.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ToolRequest {
    pub id: String,
    pub tool_type: String,      // "edit", "run", "build"
    pub parameters: serde_json::Value,
}

/// Returns a JSON‑encoded response for the orchestrator.
pub async fn execute_tool(req: ToolRequest) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    match req.tool_type.as_str() {
        "edit" => edit_file(req).await,
        "run" => run_repl(req).await,
        "build" => run_build(req).await,
        _ => Err(anyhow::anyhow!("Unsupported tool_type")),
    }
}

async fn edit_file(req: ToolRequest) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    let path = req.parameters["path"]
        .as_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Missing path"))?;
    let content = req.parameters["content"]
        .as_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Missing content"))?;
    fs::write(path, content)?;
    Ok(serde_json::json!({"status":"ok"}))
}

async fn run_repl(req: ToolRequest) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    let language = req.parameters["language"]
        .as_str()
        .unwrap_or("python");
    let code = req.parameters["code"]
        .as_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Missing code"))?;

    // Simple REPL execution using subprocess.
    let output = Command::new(match language {
            "python" => "python3",
            "node" => "node",
            "bash" => "bash",
            _ => return Err(anyhow::anyhow!("Unsupported language")),
        })
        .arg("-c")
        .arg(code)
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
        .output()?;

    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
    Ok(serde_json::json!({
        "stdout": stdout,
        "stderr": stderr,
        "exit_code": output.status.code()
    }))
}

async fn run_build(_req: ToolRequest) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    // Trigger Nixpacks build via a CLI call.
    let status = Command::new("nixpacks")
        .arg("build")
        .arg("--config")
        .arg("/config/nixpacks")
        .status()?;
    Ok(serde_json::json!({"build_success": status.success()}))
}
```

```js
import { chromium } from "playwright";
import axios from "axios";

/**
 * Entry point called by the orchestrator via HTTP.
 * Expected payload:
 * {
 *   "taskId": "<uuid>",
 *   "previewUrl": "",
 *   "testPlan": "auto" // or explicit steps
 * }
 */
export async function run(task) {
  const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page = await context.newPage();

  // Video capture for observability
  await page.evaluate(() => console.log("Starting test run"));
  const videoPath = `/tmp/video-${task.taskId}.webm`;
  await context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true, sources: true });

  try {
    await page.goto(task.previewUrl, { waitUntil: "networkidle" });
    // Simple heuristic: click all buttons with non‑empty ARIA labels
    const buttons = await page.$$('[role="button"][aria-label]');
    for (const btn of buttons) {
      const label = await btn.getAttribute("aria-label");
      console.log(`Clicking button ${label}`);
      await btn.click({ force: true });
    }
    // Capture success state – look for a DOM element with data-test="ready"
    const ready = await page.$('[data-test="ready"]');
    const success = !!ready;
    await page.screenshot({ path: `/tmp/screenshot-${task.taskId}.png` });
    await context.tracing.stop({ path: `/tmp/trace-${task.taskId}.zip` });

    // Post result back to orchestrator
    await axios.post("", {
      taskId: task.taskId,
      success,
      videoPath,
      screenshotPath: `/tmp/screenshot-${task.taskId}.png`,
```

```hcl
# Features: Autoscaling warm pools, Workload Identity, Binary Auth

resource "google_container_cluster" "primary" {
  provider = google-beta
  
  name     = "ai-engineer-gke"
  location = var.gcp_region
  
  # Use VPC-native networking

  network         = google_compute_network.vpc.id
  subnetwork      = google_compute_subnetwork.gke_subnet.id

  # Regional cluster for HA (multi-zone)
  node_locations = var.gke_node_zones

  # Remove default node pool immediately
  remove_default_node_pool = true
  initial_node_count       = 1

  # Release channel for automatic updates
  release_channel {
    channel = "REGULAR"
  }

  # Workload Identity for secure GCP API access
  workload_identity_config {
    workload_pool = "${var.gcp_project}.svc.id.goog"
  }

  # IP allocation for pods and services
  ip_allocation_policy {
    cluster_secondary_range_name  = "gke-pods"
    services_secondary_range_name = "gke-services"
  }

  # Maintenance window (Sunday 3-5 AM UTC)
  maintenance_policy {
    daily_maintenance_window {
      start_time = "03:00"
    }
  }

  # Binary Authorization for container image validation
  binary_authorization {
    evaluation_mode = "PROJECT_SINGLETON_POLICY_ENFORCE"
  }

  # Network policy enabled
  network_policy {
    enabled  = true
    provider = "PROVIDER_UNSPECIFIED"
  }

  # Master authorized networks (restrict access)
  master_authorized_networks_config {
    cidr_blocks {
      cidr_block   = "0.0.0.0/0"  # Restrict in production
      display_name = "all"
    }
  }

  # Cluster autoscaling configuration
  cluster_autoscaling {
    enabled = true
    
    resource_limits {
      resource_type = "cpu"
      minimum       = 8
      maximum       = 200
    }
    
    resource_limits {
      resource_type = "memory"
      minimum       = 32
      maximum       = 800
    }

    auto_provisioning_defaults {
      oauth_scopes = [
        ""
      ]
      
      service_account = google_service_account.gke_nodes.email
      
      management {
        auto_repair  = true
        auto_upgrade = true
      }

      shielded_instance_config {
        enable_secure_boot          = true
        enable_integrity_monitoring = true
      }
    }
  }

  # Monitoring and logging
  monitoring_config {
    enable_components = ["SYSTEM_COMPONENTS", "WORKLOADS"]
    
    managed_prometheus {
      enabled = true
    }
  }

  logging_config {
    enable_components = ["SYSTEM_COMPONENTS", "WORKLOADS"]
  }

  # Addons
  addons_config {
    http_load_balancing {
      disabled = false
    }
    
    horizontal_pod_autoscaling {
      disabled = false
    }
    
    network_policy_config {
      disabled = false
    }
    
    gcp_filestore_csi_driver_config {
      enabled = true
    }
  }

  # Cost allocation tags
  resource_labels = {
    environment = "production"
    managed_by  = "terraform"
    project     = "ai-engineer"
  }

  depends_on = [
    google_compute_subnetwork.gke_subnet
  ]
}

  database_version = "POSTGRES_15"
  region           = var.gcp_region

  depends_on = [google_service_networking_connection.private_vpc_connection]

    tier              = "db-custom-4-16384"  # 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM
    availability_type = "REGIONAL"  # High Availability mode
    disk_type         = "PD_SSD"
    disk_size         = 100
    disk_autoresize   = true
    disk_autoresize_limit = 500

    # Backup configuration
    backup_configuration {
      enabled                        = true
      start_time                     = "02:00"  # Daily backup at 2 AM UTC
      point_in_time_recovery_enabled = true
      transaction_log_retention_days = 7
      
      backup_retention_settings {
        retained_backups = 30
        retention_unit   = "COUNT"
      }
    }

    # Maintenance window
    maintenance_window {
      day          = 7  # Sunday
      hour         = 3  # 3 AM UTC
      update_track = "stable"
    }

    # IP configuration - private only
    ip_configuration {
      ipv4_enabled    = false  # No public IP
      private_network = google_compute_network.vpc.id
      require_ssl     = true
      
      # SSL mode
      ssl_mode = "ENCRYPTED_ONLY"
    }

    # Database flags for performance
    database_flags {
      name  = "max_connections"
      value = "500"
    }
    
    database_flags {
      name  = "shared_buffers"
      value = "4096000"  # 4 GB
    }
    
    database_flags {
      name  = "effective_cache_size"
      value = "12288000"  # 12 GB
    }
    
    database_flags {
      name  = "work_mem"
      value = "16384"  # 16 MB
    }
    
    database_flags {
      name  = "maintenance_work_mem"
      value = "2097152"  # 2 GB
    }
    
    database_flags {
      name  = "max_wal_size"
      value = "2048"  # 2 GB
    }

    # Insights configuration
    insights_config {
      query_insights_enabled  = true
      query_plans_per_minute  = 5
      query_string_length     = 1024
      record_application_tags = true
    }

    # Deletion protection
    deletion_protection_enabled = true
  }

  # Deletion protection at resource level
  deletion_protection = true
}
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# AI ENGINEER AGENT ENTRYPOINT
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

set -euo pipefail

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LOGGING UTILITIES
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

log_info() {
    echo "[$(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [INFO] $*"
}

log_error() {
    echo "[$(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [ERROR] $*" >&2
}

log_warn() {
    echo "[$(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [WARN] $*"
}

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE VALIDATION
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

validate_env() {
    local required_vars=(
        "TEMPORAL_HOSTPORT"
        "POSTGRES_HOST"
        "POSTGRES_DB"
        "POSTGRES_USER"
    )
    
    local missing_vars=()
    
    for var in "${required_vars[@]}"; do
        if [[ -z "${!var:-}" ]]; then
            missing_vars+=("$var")
        fi
    done
    
    if [[ ${#missing_vars[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        log_error "Missing required environment variables: ${missing_vars[*]}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    log_info "Environment validation passed"
    return 0
}

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SECRET FETCHING FROM VAULT / SECRET MANAGER
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fetch_secrets() {
    log_info "Fetching secrets from secret manager..."
    
    # Check if running in GCP with Workload Identity
    if [[ -n "${GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS:-}" ]] || [[ -f "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token" ]]; then
        log_info "Detected GCP environment - using Secret Manager"
        
        # Fetch database password if not already set
        if [[ -z "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-}" ]]; then
            export POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret="postgres-password" 2>/dev/null || echo "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD_DEFAULT}")
        fi
        
        # Fetch OpenAI API key
        if [[ -z "${OPENAI_API_KEY:-}" ]]; then
            export OPENAI_API_KEY=$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret="openai-api-key" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        fi
    else
        log_warn "No secret manager detected - using environment variables"
```

```go
func AgentWorkflow(ctx workflow.Context, input AgentWorkflowInput) error {
	logger := workflow.GetLogger(ctx)
	
	// Workflow start time for timeout enforcement

	workflowsStarted.Inc()
	
	logger.Info("Starting Agent Workflow",

	}
	
	ctx = workflow.WithWorkflowRunTimeout(ctx, input.MaxDuration)
	
	// Initialize workflow state

	var failedTasks int
	var allResults []TaskResult
	
	// Main workflow loop - continues until planner signals completion or timeout
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			elapsed := workflow.Now(ctx).Sub(startTime)
			logger.Info("Workflow timeout or cancellation",
				"elapsed", elapsed,
				"completed_tasks", completedTasks,
				"failed_tasks", failedTasks)
			
			workflowDuration.Observe(elapsed.Seconds())
			workflowsCompleted.WithLabelValues("timeout").Inc()
			return ctx.Err()
			
		default:
			// Get next tasks from planner
			plannerResp, err := callPlanner(ctx, input.SessionID, allResults)
			if err != nil {
				logger.Error("Planner call failed", "error", err)
				workflowsCompleted.WithLabelValues("error").Inc()
				return err
			}
			
			// Check if planner signals completion
			if plannerResp.Complete {
				elapsed := workflow.Now(ctx).Sub(startTime)
				logger.Info("Workflow completed by planner",
					"elapsed", elapsed,
					"completed_tasks", completedTasks,
					"failed_tasks", failedTasks,
					"reasoning", plannerResp.Reasoning)
				
				workflowDuration.Observe(elapsed.Seconds())
				workflowsCompleted.WithLabelValues("success").Inc()
				return nil
			}
			
			// Execute tasks in parallel
			if len(plannerResp.Tasks) > 0 {
				results := executeTasksInParallel(ctx, plannerResp.Tasks)
				
				for _, result := range results {
					allResults = append(allResults, result)
					if result.Success {
						completedTasks++
					} else {
						failedTasks++
					}
				}
			}
			
			// Brief sleep to prevent tight loop
			_ = workflow.Sleep(ctx, 5*time.Second)
		}
	}

func executeTasksInParallel(ctx workflow.Context, tasks []TaskDescriptor) []TaskResult {
	logger := workflow.GetLogger(ctx)
	
	logger.Info("Executing tasks in parallel", "count", len(tasks))
	
	// Create selectors for parallel execution
	selector := workflow.NewSelector(ctx)
	pendingTasks := make(map[string]workflow.Future)
	results := make([]TaskResult, 0, len(tasks))
	
	// Start all tasks
	for _, task := range tasks {
		future := executeTask(ctx, task)
		pendingTasks[task.ID] = future
		
		// Add to selector
		selector.AddFuture(future, func(f workflow.Future) {
			var result TaskResult
			err := f.Get(ctx, &result)
			if err != nil {
				logger.Error("Task execution failed", "task_id", task.ID, "error", err)
				result = TaskResult{
					TaskID:  task.ID,
					Success: false,
					Error:   err.Error(),
				}
			}
			results = append(results, result)
			delete(pendingTasks, task.ID)
		})
	}
	
	// Wait for all tasks to complete
	for len(pendingTasks) > 0 {
		selector.Select(ctx)
	}
	
	logger.Info("All tasks completed", "count", len(results))
	return results
}
```

```python
        self.max_tasks_per_iteration = int(os.getenv("MAX_TASKS_PER_ITERATION", "5"))
    
    async def plan_next_tasks(
        self,
        session_id: str,
        user_prompt: str,
        previous_results: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    ) -> PlannerResponse:
        """
        Generate next set of tasks based on user prompt and previous results.
        Implements hierarchical planning: strategy → tactics → tasks.
        """
        
        # Step 1: Policy enforcement via Decision-Time Guidance
        logger.info(f"[{session_id}] Evaluating policy for prompt: {user_prompt[:100]}...")
        
        try:
            allowed, micro_instruction = self.guidance.evaluate(user_prompt, session_id)
            if not allowed:
                raise PolicyViolationError("Request blocked by security policy")
            
            if micro_instruction:
                logger.info(f"[{session_id}] Policy guidance: {micro_instruction}")
        except PolicyViolationError as e:
            logger.error(f"[{session_id}] Policy violation: {e}")
            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=str(e))
        
        # Step 2: Analyze previous results to determine progress
        progress_summary = self._analyze_progress(previous_results)
        
        # Step 3: Check if objective is complete
        if self._check_completion(user_prompt, previous_results, context):
            logger.info(f"[{session_id}] Objective complete - no more tasks")
            return PlannerResponse(
                tasks=[],
                complete=True,
                reasoning="User objective has been fully achieved based on previous task results.",
                confidence=0.95
            )
        
        # Step 4: Generate high-level strategy
        strategy = await self._generate_strategy(user_prompt, progress_summary, context)
        
        # Step 5: Decompose strategy into atomic tasks
        tasks = await self._decompose_to_tasks(strategy, micro_instruction)
        
        # Step 6: Validate and prioritize tasks
        tasks = self._validate_tasks(tasks)
        tasks = self._prioritize_tasks(tasks)
        
        # Step 7: Limit to max tasks per iteration
        tasks = tasks[:self.max_tasks_per_iteration]
        
        # Step 8: Calculate estimated duration
        total_duration = sum(t.estimated_duration_minutes or 5.0 for t in tasks)
        
        logger.info(f"[{session_id}] Generated {len(tasks)} tasks, estimated duration: {total_duration} min")
        
        return PlannerResponse(
            tasks=tasks,
            complete=False,
            reasoning=strategy,
            confidence=0.85,
            estimated_total_duration_minutes=total_duration
        )
    
    def _analyze_progress(self, previous_results: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
        """Analyze previous task results to summarize progress"""
        if not previous_results:
            return "No previous tasks executed yet."
        
        successful = sum(1 for r in previous_results if r.get("success"))
        failed = len(previous_results) - successful
        
        recent_outputs = [r.get("output", "") for r in previous_results[-3:]]
        recent_summary = " | ".join(recent_outputs)
        
        return (
            f"Progress: {successful} successful tasks, {failed} failed. "
            f"Recent outputs: {recent_summary}"
        )
    
    def _check_completion(
        self,
        user_prompt: str,
        previous_results: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Determine if user objective is complete.
        Uses LLM to evaluate if recent outputs satisfy original prompt.
        """
        if not previous_results:
            return False
        
        # Simple heuristic: if last 3 tasks all succeeded and outputs indicate completion
        recent_results = previous_results[-3:]
        all_success = all(r.get("success") for r in recent_results)
        
        if not all_success:
            return False
        
        # Check outputs for completion indicators
        completion_keywords = ["completed", "finished", "done", "deployed", "passed all tests"]
        recent_outputs = " ".join(r.get("output", "").lower() for r in recent_results)
        
        return any(keyword in recent_outputs for keyword in completion_keywords)

        user_message = f"""User Request: {user_prompt}

Current Progress: {progress_summary}

Context: {json.dumps(context) if context else "None"}

Generate a strategic plan for the next iteration."""
        
        try:
            response = self.client.chat.completions.create(
                model=self.model,
                messages=[
                    {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
                    {"role": "user", "content": user_message}
                ],

            )
```

```python
"""services/planner/src/decision_guidance.py"""

import yaml
import numpy as np
from typing import Tuple, Optional, List, Dict
import logging
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class PolicyViolationError(Exception):
    """Raised when a request violates security policy"""
    pass

class DecisionGuidance:
    """
    Lightweight multi-label classifier for runtime policy decisions.
    
    Determines if a user prompt is allowed and optionally returns
    a short micro-instruction (max 2 sentences) to guide execution.
    
    The model is loaded from a YAML file containing:
    - Feature vectorization rules (bag-of-words tokens)
    - Logistic regression coefficients
    - Micro-instruction templates
    
    Evaluation is deterministic and completes in <1ms.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model_path: str):
        """
        Initialize Decision Guidance from YAML configuration.
        
        Args:
            model_path: Path to YAML config file with model weights
        """
        logger.info(f"Loading Decision Guidance policy from: {model_path}")
        
        try:
            with open(model_path, "r") as f:
                config = yaml.safe_load(f)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to load policy config: {e}")
            raise
        
        # Extract configuration
        self.vectorizer_config = config["vectorizer"]
        self.model_params = config["model_params"]
        self.coefficients = np.array(config["coefficients"])
        self.intercept = np.array(config["intercept"])
        self.micro_instructions = config["micro_instructions"]
        
        # Initialize logistic regression model with pre-trained weights
        self.model = LogisticRegression(**self.model_params)
        self.model.coef_ = self.coefficients
        self.model.intercept_ = self.intercept
        self.model.classes_ = np.array([0, 1])  # 0 = deny, 1 = allow
        
        # Pre-compile token list for faster lookup
        self.tokens = self.vectorizer_config["tokens"]
        self.allow_threshold = self.vectorizer_config["allow_threshold"]
        
        logger.info(f"Policy loaded: {len(self.tokens)} features, threshold={self.allow_threshold}")
    
    def _featurize(self, text: str) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Convert text to feature vector using bag-of-words.
        
        Simple token counting approach:
        - Count occurrences of each token in lowercase text
        - Return feature vector matching model input dimensions
        
        Args:
            text: Input prompt text
            
        Returns:
            Feature vector of shape (1, n_features)
        """
        text_lower = text.lower()
        
        # Count token occurrences
        features = [text_lower.count(token) for token in self.tokens]
        
        # Reshape to (1, n_features) for model input
        return np.array(features, dtype=np.float32).reshape(1, -1)
    
    def evaluate(self, text: str, session_id: str) -> Tuple[bool, Optional[str]]:
        """
        Evaluate if prompt is allowed and select micro-instruction.
        
        Process:
        1. Featurize input text
        2. Predict probability of "allow" class
        3. Compare to threshold
        4. Select appropriate micro-instruction based on confidence
        
        Args:
            text: User prompt to evaluate
            session_id: Session identifier for logging
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (allowed: bool, micro_instruction: str|None)
            
        Raises:
            PolicyViolationError: If prompt is blocked by policy
        """
        # Featurize input
        X = self._featurize(text)
        
        # Predict probability
        try:
            proba = self.model.predict_proba(X)[0, 1]  # Probability of "allow" class
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"[{session_id}] Prediction failed: {e}")
            # Fail-safe: deny on error
            return False, None
        
        logger.debug(f"[{session_id}] Policy score: {proba:.3f} (threshold: {self.allow_threshold})")
        
        # Decision based on threshold
        allowed = proba >= self.allow_threshold
        
        if not allowed:
            logger.warning(f"[{session_id}] Policy DENIED prompt (score: {proba:.3f})")
            return False, None
        
        # Select micro-instruction based on confidence level
        micro_instr = self._select_micro_instruction(proba)
        
        if micro_instr:
            logger.info(f"[{session_id}] Policy ALLOWED with guidance: {micro_instr}")
        else:
            logger.info(f"[{session_id}] Policy ALLOWED (score: {proba:.3f})")
        
        return True, micro_instr
    
    def _select_micro_instruction(self, confidence: float) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Select appropriate micro-instruction based on confidence score.
        
        Confidence ranges:
        - < 0.7: High caution - restrict operations
        - 0.7-0.9: Moderate caution - proceed with care
        - > 0.9: High confidence - full access
        
        Args:
            confidence: Probability score from model (0.0-1.0)
            
        Returns:
            Micro-instruction string or None for high confidence
        """
        if confidence < 0.7:
            # High caution - strict restrictions
            return np.random.choice(self.micro_instructions.get("high_caution", [
                "Proceed with extreme caution. Limit file writes to /tmp only."
            ]))
        
        elif confidence < 0.9:
            # Moderate caution - general guidance
            return np.random.choice(self.micro_instructions.get("caution", [
                "Proceed but limit file writes to the /tmp directory.",
                "Avoid executing external commands."
            ]))
        
        else:
            # High confidence - no restrictions needed
            # Optionally return encouraging message
            if np.random.random() < 0.1:  # 10% of the time
                return np.random.choice(self.micro_instructions.get("optimistic", [
                    "Full access granted; continue as requested."
                ]))
            return None
    
    def get_policy_summary(self) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """
        Return summary of loaded policy configuration.
        
        Useful for debugging and observability.
        """
        return {
            "num_features": len(self.tokens),
            "allow_threshold": self.allow_threshold,
            "model_type": "LogisticRegression",
            "instruction_categories": list(self.micro_instructions.keys()),
            "coefficients_shape": self.coefficients.shape
        }
```

```rust
            ToolParams::Read { path } => {
                self.handle_read(&path).await?
            }
        };
        
        Ok(ToolResponse {
            request_id: request.id,
            result_json,
        })
    }
    
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // FILE EDIT OPERATION
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    
    async fn handle_edit(&self, path: &str, content: &str, create_dirs: bool) -> Result<String> {
        info!("Handling edit request: path={}", path);
        
        // Validate path is within workspace (sandbox check)
        let full_path = self.validate_path(path)?;
        
        // Create parent directories if requested
        if create_dirs {
            if let Some(parent) = full_path.parent() {
                fs::create_dir_all(parent)
                    .with_context(|| format!("Failed to create directories for {}", path))?;
            }
        }
        
        // Write file content
        fs::write(&full_path, content)
            .with_context(|| format!("Failed to write file: {}", path))?;
        
        info!("File written successfully: {}", path);
        
        Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "status": "success",
            "path": path,
            "bytes_written": content.len()
        }).to_string())
    }
    
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // FILE READ OPERATION
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    
    async fn handle_read(&self, path: &str) -> Result<String> {
        debug!("Handling read request: path={}", path);
        
        let full_path = self.validate_path(path)?;
        
        let content = fs::read_to_string(&full_path)
            .with_context(|| format!("Failed to read file: {}", path))?;
        
        Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "status": "success",
            "path": path,
            "content": content,
            "bytes_read": content.len()
        }).to_string())
    }
    
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // CODE EXECUTION (REPL)
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    
    async fn handle_run(&self, language: &str, code: &str, timeout: u64) -> Result<String> {
        info!("Handling run request: language={}, timeout={}s", language, timeout);
        
        let (interpreter, args) = match language.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            "python" | "python3" => ("python3", vec!["-c"]),
            "node" | "javascript" | "js" => ("node", vec!["-e"]),
            "bash" | "sh" => ("bash", vec!["-c"]),
            "ruby" => ("ruby", vec!["-e"]),
            _ => return Err(anyhow!("Unsupported language: {}", language)),
        };
        
        // Execute with timeout
        let output = tokio::time::timeout(
            tokio::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout),
            TokioCommand::new(interpreter)
                .args(&args)
                .arg(code)
                .stdout(Stdio::piped())
                .stderr(Stdio::piped())
                .output()
        ).await
            .context("Execution timeout")?
            .context("Failed to execute command")?;
        
        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();
        let exit_code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);
        
        debug!("Execution completed: exit_code={}", exit_code);
        
        Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "status": if exit_code == 0 { "success" } else { "error" },
            "stdout": stdout,
            "stderr": stderr,
            "exit_code": exit_code
        }).to_string())
    }
    
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // BUILD OPERATION (Nixpacks/Docker)
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    
    async fn handle_build(&self, build_system: Option<&str>, config_path: Option<&str>) -> Result<String> {
        info!("Handling build request: system={:?}", build_system);
        
        let system = build_system.unwrap_or("nixpacks");
        
        let output = match system {
            "nixpacks" => {
                let config = config_path.unwrap_or("/opt/config/nixpacks");
                TokioCommand::new("nixpacks")
                    .args(&["build", "--config", config, "."])
                    .current_dir(&self.workspace_root)
                    .stdout(Stdio::piped())
                    .stderr(Stdio::piped())
                    .output()
                    .await
                    .context("Nixpacks build failed")?
            }
            
            "docker" => {
                TokioCommand::new("docker")
                    .args(&["build", "-t", "ai-engineer-app:latest", "."])
                    .current_dir(&self.workspace_root)
                    .stdout(Stdio::piped())
                    .stderr(Stdio::piped())
                    .output()
                    .await
                    .context("Docker build failed")?
            }
            
            _ => return Err(anyhow!("Unsupported build system: {}", system))
        };
        
        let success = output.status.success();
        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();
        
        Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "status": if success { "success" } else { "error" },
            "build_system": system,
            "stdout": stdout,
            "stderr": stderr,
            "build_success": success
        }).to_string())
    }
    
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // SECURITY: PATH VALIDATION
    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    
    fn validate_path(&self, path: &str) -> Result<PathBuf> {
        // Normalize path
        let full_path = if path.starts_with('/') {
            PathBuf::from(path)
        } else {
            self.workspace_root.join(path)
        };
        
        // Canonicalize to resolve .. and symlinks
        let canonical = full_path.canonicalize()
            .or_else(|_| {
                // If file doesn't exist yet, validate parent
                if let Some(parent) = full_path.parent() {
                    parent.canonicalize().map(|p| p.join(full_path.file_name().unwrap()))
                } else {
                    Ok(full_path.clone())
                }
            })?;
        
        // Sandbox check: ensure path is within workspace
        if self.sandbox_enabled && !canonical.starts_with(&self.workspace_root) {
            warn!("Path validation failed: {} outside workspace", path);
            return Err(anyhow!("Access denied: path outside workspace"));
        }
        
        Ok(canonical)
    }
}
```
